title: Costco, Cracker Barrel, and a Trump-Xi Summit: Your Week Ahead
description: A packed week of earnings from Costco, Darden, Lennar, and AutoZone lands right after the Fed's September meeting, alongside fresh housing and sentiment data. Alex and Jordan map out what to watch, including the high-stakes Trump-Xi summit that could move markets either direction.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Welcome back to Under the Radar, everybody. It's September 20th, and honestly, this coming week has a little bit of everything -- earnings, housing data, Fed speakers, and a geopolitical summit that could swing markets in either direction.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Yeah, this is one of those weeks where the calendar just looks stacked from Monday morning to Friday afternoon. Let's start with earnings, because there are a lot of names to get through.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Monday after the close we've got Stitch Fix, Cracker Barrel, and MillerKnoll all reporting. None of those are going to be huge market movers on their own, but Cracker Barrel's worth a glance just given how much attention that brand's gotten this year.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Then Tuesday is where it really picks up. AutoZone and General Mills both report before the open, and you've also got Thor Industries, Worthington Enterprises, and KB Home in the mix that same day.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: AutoZone and General Mills are an interesting pair to think about together, actually. One's auto parts, one's packaged food, but they're both kind of a read on how resilient the everyday consumer still is. Are people still fixing up their old cars instead of buying new ones? Are they trading down on groceries?

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: And KB Home and Lennar later in the week give you two looks at homebuilders in the same seven-day stretch, which pairs nicely with New Home Sales data landing Thursday morning. We'll come back to that housing cluster in a bit because there's a lot stacked on that one day.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Wednesday's a little lighter -- Dave & Buster's reports, consensus is looking for around eighty-five cents a share. Not exactly a market-mover, but worth watching if you're tracking the discretionary entertainment spending trend.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Then Thursday is the big one. Darden and Paychex report before the open, TD SYNNEX is also on the docket, and then after the close you've got Costco, Lennar, and Abivax.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Costco is the marquee name of the entire week, honestly. It's late September, we're heading into the holiday shopping season, and Costco membership trends and spending patterns are about as good a real-time read on the consumer as you're going to get from any single company.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Darden's worth sitting with too, because restaurant spending tends to be one of the first things people pull back on when they're feeling squeezed. If Darden's commentary on traffic and check sizes is soft, that's a signal worth taking seriously.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: And then Friday's pretty quiet on the earnings side -- just some smaller names like RF Industries and Coda Octopus. Nothing there that's likely to move the broader market.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Okay, so that's the earnings side. Let's talk economic data, because there's actually a really coherent story if you connect the dots this week.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Tuesday we get the Richmond Fed Manufacturing Index for September. Wednesday brings the flash S&P Global Manufacturing and Services PMIs, which is one of the earliest looks we get at how the economy's tracking this month.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Thursday's the housing day I mentioned -- New Home Sales for August comes out that morning, and then Lennar reports earnings that same evening. So you get the data and the company commentary almost back to back, which is a nice little natural experiment if the numbers disagree with each other.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: And Friday closes the week with Durable Goods Orders for August and the final University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment reading for September. That sentiment number is one I'd flag especially -- confidence readings have been running pretty weak all year, so any real move there, up or down, is going to get attention.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: One thing worth being clear on: Core PCE, the Fed's favorite inflation gauge, does not come out this week. That's not until September 30th, so that's a story for next week's episode, not this one.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Good to flag, because I think some people might assume it's coming given how much Fed talk there's going to be. And there will be a lot of Fed talk, because this is all landing right in the wake of the September FOMC meeting.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Right, the meeting wrapped up on the 16th with the press conference and the updated projections, so this week you've got a bunch of Fed officials out on the circuit reacting to and clarifying what actually got decided.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Which is always a fun little exercise, because you get the official statement, and then you get five different Fed presidents giving five slightly different flavors of commentary on it.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: It's basically a 'what did the Fed really say' game every time. But it matters here because markets are going to be parsing every word for hints on the pace of further cuts heading into that final FOMC meeting of the year.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Now, if we're talking about the single biggest event of the week, though, it's not earnings and it's not a Fed speaker -- it's the Trump-Xi summit.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: This is the one I think everyone's going to be watching closest. Trump's sitting down with Xi Jinping at the White House, covering everything from tariffs to technology, and this follows up on their May summit over in Beijing.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: And the risk here really does cut both ways. If there's any concrete signal on trade or tariff de-escalation, or something like agricultural purchase commitments, that could be a real upside catalyst for markets.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: But if talks break down or come across as contentious, that's downside risk in the other direction. It's genuinely a coin flip in terms of market reaction, which makes it the wildcard of the week.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: So if I'm summarizing the week for someone who only has two minutes: Costco Thursday night is your consumer spending read heading into the holidays, Darden and Lennar give you restaurant and housing color, and then the Trump-Xi summit is the geopolitical wildcard that could overshadow all of it.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: And don't sleep on Friday's consumer sentiment number either. Given how weak those readings have been running, a surprise in either direction could shift the conversation about where the consumer really stands heading into Q4.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Layer in the Fed speakers threading through the whole week reacting to the September meeting, and yeah -- there's a lot to keep an eye on, but it all kind of ties together around one question: how healthy is the consumer, and how is the Fed thinking about that as we head toward year-end.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: That's a great way to frame it. Alright, before we wrap up, let's get the disclaimer out of the way.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Quick reminder before we get into it: everything in this episode is for informational and entertainment purposes only. It is not financial advice, and you should always do your own research or talk to a licensed financial advisor before making investment decisions.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Well said. Thanks for hanging out with us today, everyone -- we'll be back next week to break down how all of this actually played out. Take care, and we'll catch you then.
